properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 17 at 7:38PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Heavy rain and strong winds are expected to start Friday and last
through the weekend as multiple strong low pressure systems move
into the northern gulf. These lows will bring multiple days of
moderate to heavy rain, with around 1.5 to 3 inches of rain every 24
hours. Some areas, especially near Yakutat and along the gulf coast,
could see localized areas reach around 4 inches of rain in 24 hours.
Heaviest rain rates are anticipated late Saturday into Sunday with
hourly rates of 0.15 to 0.3 inches possible. This heavy rain will
likely cause rapid river rises along smaller rivers and streams, but
no flooding is expected at this time.

Along with this heavy rain, increased winds are highly likely across
the area. Strongest winds are anticipated to occur late Saturday
into Sunday with 30 to 40 kts, gusts to 50 kts across the gulf and
20 to 35 kts, gusts around 40 to 50 kts across the northern inner
channels. Land winds will also increase, with areas especially along
the gulf coast seeing wind gusts up to around 45 mph. Check back for
more updates through the weekend.

Counties.

July, and on September 15 reached flood stage.  The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a

hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

stage at 28.2 feet.

feet on 10/05/1965.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 106.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Illinois and

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion
and heat stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety
and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks
in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

People in the Saint Louis Metropolitan Area can get information about
cooling centers or energy assistance related to the excessive heat by
calling the United Way of Greater Saint Louis at 800-427-4626, or if
calling from a land line phone dial 2-1-1. You can also call Cool
Down Saint Louis at 314-241-7668.

properties.description:
The St. Louis Clean Air Partnership has issued an air quality alert
for the St. Louis metropolitan area from 10 AM to 8 PM CDT Friday.

An Orange air quality forecast means that maximum ozone
concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/

...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WITH GUSTY WINDS AND LITTLE RAINFALL...

A strong low pressure system in northeastern California will
bring scattered thunderstorms this afternoon and evening with
outflow wind gusts up to 50 mph and little rainfall. As the low
moves into southeastern Oregon late tonight and southwestern
Idaho on Friday, scattered thunderstorms will develop again,
especially on the Idaho side.

Watch for winds and low relative humidities, which is in effect
from late tonight through Friday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zones 403 Northern
Boise National Forest, 421 Southern Boise/Western Sawtooth NF
and including the Camas Prairie.

* TIMING...For the Red Flag Warning, until 9 PM MDT this
evening. For the Fire Weather Watch, from late tonight through
Friday evening.

* WINDS...For the Fire Weather Watch, Northwest 5 to 10 mph with
gusts up to 25 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...For the Fire Weather Watch, 39 to 53
percent.

* TEMPERATURES...For the Fire Weather Watch, 56 to 68 degrees.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 50 mph.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will occur shortly.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

properties.description:
ESFLOT

Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms are possible starting
late Friday night and continuing into Monday across southern
Wisconsin, northern Illinois, and part of northwestern Indiana. High
moisture content in the atmosphere will lead to torrential downpours
where thunderstorms are most frequent, leading to the potential for
several inches of rain on a widespread basis.

The favored area for several rounds of showers and thunderstorms
Friday night through Monday will be near and north of Interstate 80
where several inches of rain have fallen in the past 24 hours. The
intersection of increasingly saturated soils and repeated downpours
may lead to areas of flooding and rises in river levels, including
along the Rock, Fox, DuPage, and Illinois rivers.

This outlook means that elevated water levels and potential impacts
are possible, but not yet certain. Persons should closely monitor
forecasts including the possibility of flood watches, warnings, and
advisories.

Additional statements or outlooks may be issued by tomorrow morning.
